source.title: Universal Reasoner: A Single, Composable Plug-and-Play Reasoner for Frozen LLMs
source.authors: Jaemin Kim; Hangeol Chang; Hyunmin Hwang; Choonghan Kim; Jong Chul Ye

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no cut-off or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper presents results for reward-trained reasoning modules guiding frozen larger models, but does not test fine-tuning a strong student on labels produced by a weaker supervisor or measure PGR. Its transfer results are a related, different setup.
record.gate_note: The paper uses the phrase weak-to-strong generalization for transferring a smaller reasoning module to a larger frozen backbone. The module is trained with verifiable rewards, not weaker-model labels; the backbone is guided by logit addition rather than fine-tuned on those labels. The transfer and guidance results below therefore bear on a related construct, not V1–V6. Other comparisons of UniR with GRPO or guidance methods are not extracted unless they show this related transfer outcome.
record.test_reason: UniR trains a small module with verifiable (ground-truth) rewards and adds its logits to a frozen larger backbone at inference. No strong model is trained on a weaker model's labels, and there is no weak supervisor accuracy, strong ceiling or PGR. The paper calls this 'weak-to-strong generalization', but the construct is small-to-large guidance transfer, not weak-label supervision.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that UniR, a plug-and-play reasoning module trained on verifiable rewards, outperforms GRPO fine-tuning, is more robust to sampling temperature, and transfers to larger backbones, VLMs and the medical domain. They also conclude that modules compose by summing logits. Their use of 'weak-to-strong generalization' means small-to-large module transfer, not weak-label supervision.
record.recipe_differences: UniR trains a separate reasoning module using verifiable rewards and combines its logits with a frozen backbone at inference; it does not fine-tune a strong model on labels generated by a weaker model.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports cross-tokenizer alignment as a condition affecting outcome: the trained module improves over an untrained module but remains below the backbone-only score. It also reports transfer across backbone/module sizes and tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: A small module trained with verifiable rewards alongside a 3B backbone, then added at the logit level, raises the average math score of frozen larger backbones. Averages rise from 33.7 to 35.5 and from 51.1 to 53.6 for the 8B/14B backbones, and from 51.1 to 52.8 with a 0.5B module on the 14B backbone. Guidance also helps a frozen VLM. Cross-tokenizer guidance falls below backbone-only (35.6 to 18.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small reward-trained guidance modules transfer to larger frozen backbones via logit addition, with modest gains when tokenizers are shared and losses under imperfect cross-tokenizer alignment.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The core claim's weak-label intervention and PGR are not tested. The vision transfer result is reported without numeric values in the text, and the mapping between the two larger-backbone averages and the 8B/14B models is not stated in the cited passage. Cross-tokenizer transfer has a large performance drop relative to the backbone-only baseline.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for this claim were extracted. Other tables compare UniR with GRPO, other inference-time methods, or report outcomes on separate tasks without testing weak-supervisor-label fine-tuning.

untested.parts: All of it: no fine-tuning on weak-model labels, no weak supervisor or ceiling, no PGR.
All of it: no auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling of weak supervisors, or loss variants.
All of it: no PGR as a function of supervisor or student size, task, or representations.
All of it: no exploitation of the supervisor, distribution shift, or shared-error effects.
All of it: the theory covers reward decomposition into a soft Q-function, not conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
All of it: the vision experiment uses no weak supervision.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate decision is right. No verdicts are given because the study does not test any version. One possible relevance is Table 14: the 1.5B module alone scores below the 3B backbone on most benchmarks, yet the combination beats both. This is still not training on weak labels, so it is not counted.

versions.untested_parts: No strong student is fine-tuned on weaker-model labels; no weak supervisor performance, strong-model true-label ceiling, or PGR is measured.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, or weak-label loss variant is tested for PGR gains.
The paper varies reasoning-module/backbone sizes and tasks, but not weak-supervisor/student sizes or PGR; it does not test chess or compare representations as predictors of PGR.
No weak-supervisor checking failures, distribution-shift effects on weak-label fine-tuning, or shared-error effects are tested.
The theory concerns reward decomposition and optimal policies for UniR, not conditions forcing a student trained on weak labels to outperform its supervisor.
The vision-language experiment uses a text-trained reward-optimized module to guide a frozen VLM, not weak-model labels or the claimed weak-to-strong fine-tuning intervention.

rows.subject: 8B and 14B frozen backbone models (aggregate; mapping of scores to models not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Added a reasoning module trained alongside a 3B backbone as logit guidance at inference time.

conditions.value: Trained on Math-12k and GSM8k with a 3B-scale backbone

rows.baseline: 33.7 and 51.1 for the respective backbone-only baselines
rows.value: 35.5 and 53.6 for the respective transferred-module systems
rows.locator: Section 5.3, Transferability to Larger Backbone LLMs; Figure 2
rows.note: The paper reports the paired averages for the 8B and 14B evaluations but does not specify which average maps to which backbone in the text.
rows.check: This is a related construct: a reward-trained small module guides a frozen 8B/14B backbone. No weak labels are involved. From the backbone sizes and Table 1, 33.7 to 35.5 likely maps to Llama3.1-8B and 51.1 to 53.6 to Qwen2.5-14B, but the text does not state this explicitly. The state cannot be judged against any version.

rows.subject: 14B frozen backbone model (family not stated in this passage)
rows.operation_detail: Added the UniR-trained 0.5B reasoning module as inference-time guidance.
rows.note: This is a reported transfer result for the smaller module on a 14B frozen backbone, not weak-label student training.
rows.check: This is a related construct. The text labels the 51.1 baseline as the 'baseline πr', which appears to be a typo for the backbone-only score.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-3B backbone guided by Llama-3.2-1B reasoning module
rows.operation_detail: Used EVA cross-tokenizer alignment to apply a UniR-trained Llama reasoning module to a Qwen backbone.
rows.note: The text also reports 12.7 for the untrained Llama-1B module and says the trained module improves over it, while alignment imperfections lower performance below the backbone-only baseline.
rows.check: This is a related construct: cross-tokenizer guidance. The drop below backbone-only (35.6 to 18.3) is not a weak-to-strong outcome. The backbone is Qwen2.5-3B, which the paper evaluates under greedy decoding.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Added a Qwen-based 0.5B reasoning module trained on text-based GSM8k as guidance to the frozen VLM.
rows.measure: Performance on visual mathematical reasoning benchmarks
rows.baseline: Backbone-only VLM; numeric values not stated
rows.value: Figure only; the text states UniR improves performance on both benchmarks
rows.locator: Section 5.4, Extension to Vision Language Models; Figure 4
rows.note: This is a modality-transfer result with reward-optimized module guidance, not weak-supervisor labels.
rows.check: This is a related construct: a text-trained module guides a frozen VLM. It involves no weak labels, so it does not bear on V6. The values are in a figure only.
